hypothesis: Quality should be confirmed by recent industry-relative strength to avoid quality value traps. The new factor is the minimum of the R253 quality percentile and the 20-day stock-relative-to-industry percentile, so a name must be both fundamentally strong and showing positive stock-specific strength.
selection_basis: R256 showed strong discovery and validation IC without a profitable long-only portfolio. R257 changes the economic dimension rather than tuning R256: industry-relative strength is an established component of the previously researched industry-relative-strength quality sleeve. Feasibility read no forward or strategy returns: joint coverage is 99.9211% full, 99.9646% discovery, 99.8797% validation and 99.9122% recent year; 42 month-end rank correlations have mean absolute 0.113939 and maximum absolute 0.311960; the composite is 0.160932 lower than the R253 percentile on average and is at least 0.10 lower for 39.6392% of observations. Evidence: r257_data_feasibility.json.

factor.formula: quality_relative_strength_min_rank = min(rank_pct(management_ocf_gm_min_rank), rank_pct(stock_rel_industry_20d)) within same-date historical nonfinancial HS300 members; 1 is best and 0 is worst
factor.interpretation: R253 remains unchanged. R257 adds recent stock-relative-to-industry strength as the second weak link instead of changing R253's internal components, direction or score weights.
factor.pit_rule: R253 inherits its financial publication/PIT dates. stock_rel_industry_20d uses close and industry returns observable on the same trading date. Ranks and the minimum use only same-date eligible historical nonfinancial HS300 members.
factor.missing_data_rule: Both components are required; a missing component leaves the composite null.

strategies.common_filter: Current nonfinancial industry snapshot is required; history uses historical HS300 membership. Both strategies require ma60 and non-null quality_relative_strength_min_rank, so the candidate/control universe and availability are identical.
strategies.execution: 30-name score limit, at most 10 equal-weight positions, 20-day holding, -20% stop loss, T+1 open execution and 3x costs; candidate also tested at 4x/5x.

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally

segments.stitching: compound two independently run segment curves; skip the first return of each later segment

factor_ic.method: R257 factor month-end rank IC versus T+1 open to T+21 open return within historical nonfinancial HS300 members

gates.D1: full and recent-12-month joint component coverage >=0.99
gates.D2: discovery and validation joint component coverage >=0.99
gates.D3: first valid date is no later than 2023-05-04 and written values exactly match the same-date composite formula with max abs difference <=1e-12
gates.D4: mean absolute monthly component correlation <=0.70, every monthly absolute correlation <=0.80, mean composite reduction versus R253 percentile >=0.05 and at least 20% of observations reduced by >=0.10
gates.I1: discovery mean R257 rank IC >=0.02 with at least 18 month-end observations
gates.I2: validation mean R257 rank IC >=0.01 with at least 18 month-end observations and the same positive sign
gates.G2: discovery candidate MDD is no worse than control MDD by more than 5pp
gates.G4: full-sample candidate return > 0 and >= control return
gates.G5: full-sample candidate MDD <= 40% in absolute value and no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G6: rolling 1-year positive rate >= 60% and no worse than control by more than 2pp
gates.G7: recent 12-month candidate return > 0 and MDD no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G8: full-sample candidate return at 4x cost is positive
gates.G9: full-sample candidate return at 5x cost is positive
gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full sample
gates.C2: the largest symbol's share of net P&L is <= 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is <= 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is <= 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is <= 45%
gates.C7: the largest single-symbol loss is <= 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All D, I, G and C gates must pass. Any failure means the quality-relative-strength factor is not accepted and cannot be rescued by changing weights, rank direction, holding period, stop loss, universe, costs or gates after seeing results.
known_limitations: The 20-day relative-strength component can be noisy and may whipsaw.
The minimum of two percentile ranks can be sparse and sensitive to ties.
R253 and the industry-relative-strength sleeve were already researched in overlapping samples, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
The nonfinancial industry snapshot is current rather than historical PIT.
R253 inherits financial restatement and publication-timing risk.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments and segment boundaries can reset open positions.
Passing these gates would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
